Narrower than Rust. `bufferDrawBox` takes an arbitrary 11-entry custom border-glyph array plus top/bottom title text, title alignment bits and title color (buffer.rs:766-775 doc; `chars: &[u32]`, `title: Option<&str>`, `bottom_title: Option<&str>` params); node-smol picks from 4 fixed enum values (packages/tui-infra/include/tui/renderables.hpp:30-35 `enum class BorderStyle : uint8_t { kSingle = 0, kDouble = 1, kRounded = 2, kHeavy = 3, };`) and its `BoxStyle` (renderables.hpp:47-58) has no title field at all — title rendering is a genuine sub-gap inside a ported symbol.

Narrower than Rust. Rust routes through `draw_glyph` which emits a CONT_FLAG continuation cell to the right for width-2 glyphs and alpha-blends over the destination (buffer.rs:637-641 `let width = glyph_width(ch);` / `self.write_cell(x, y, ch, src_fg, src_bg, attrs);` / `if width == 2 && x + 1 < self.width {` / `self.write_cell(x + 1, y, CONT_FLAG, src_fg, src_bg, attrs);`); node-smol's `Set` is a plain bounds-checked overwrite (buffer.cc:28-33) with no continuation cell and no blending.

No table/grid border-drawing routine exists — tui-infra's renderables tier implements exactly two primitives, and neither draws grid intersections.

Narrower than Rust. node-smol advances exactly one cell per codepoint (buffer.cc:85-89 `while (p < end && col < col_end) { c.codepoint = DecodeUtf8(p, end); row[col] = c; ++col; }`), so no CJK/emoji double-width and no cluster handling; Rust's shared `draw_str` (buffer.rs:663) advances by real display width via `next_cluster` and interns multi-scalar clusters. Rust also alpha-blends and is scissor-clipped; node-smol overwrites.

No raw cell-lane pointer accessor is exposed to JS at all: node-smol stores cells as a private AoS `std::vector<Cell>` rather than stuie's four SoA lanes, so there is no char lane to hand out, and neither pointer accessor nor cell readback is bound. This is real production capability, not a bun:ffi-only helper — opentui's own buffer.ts builds live TypedArray views over these pointers (packages/core/upstream/opentui/packages/core/src/buffer.ts:86 `char: new Uint32Array(toArrayBuffer(charPtr, 0, size * 4)),`) through its platform-agnostic `platform/ffi.js` shim, and N-API has an analogue (external backing store), so out-of-scope would be wrong.
Same root cause as bufferGetCharPtr — no SoA fg-lane pointer accessor exists; node-smol's Cell stores fg inline as three uint8_t members inside a private AoS vector, with nothing bound to JS.
Ties to the same root cause as createOptimizedBuffer: there is no standalone, independently-identified buffer handle for an id string to hang on, and CellBuffer carries no id/name field.

No grapheme-cluster interning and no text readback exist in node:smol-tui, so there is no resolved-size to compute: each Cell stores exactly one raw codepoint. Unicode pre-encoding (per-codepoint width + grapheme interning) has no C++ counterpart. node-smol DOES have the width primitives (tui/width.hpp StringWidth/CodepointWidth, bound as stringWidth/codepointWidth), but nothing that encodes a string into a (width, char) array and nothing resembling the global grapheme pool, so wide/combining text still draws one cell per codepoint. Pending on the buffer/unicode tier: needs an EncodedChar-equivalent plus a grapheme pool before Buffer::DrawText can advance by display width.

Paired deallocator for encodeUnicode's leaked EncodedChar[]; since the encode step was never ported there is nothing to release. Deliberately NOT out-of-scope-as-bun:ffi: node-smol's binding does use paired create/destroy handle registries elsewhere (yogaCreateNode/yogaFreeNode, createRenderer/destroyRenderer), so a free-side symbol is a plausible shape here. Whether one is owed depends on which idiom the port picks — handle registry (needs a free) vs caller-allocated output buffer like rendererFlush (needs none) — and that design call has not been made, so "will never be ported" is not substantiable.

Diagnostics-tier symbol with no C++ counterpart; does not meet the audio / bun:ffi-no-N-API-analogue / harness-only bar (stuie's docs/interop-and-performance.md:276 names it as the example of a real 'Diagnostics' FFI category, and a plain u64 return is trivially N-API-expressible). Scope note: it is a hardcoded `0` in the Rust reference because stuie has no Zig GeneralPurposeAllocator either, so the pending work is a one-line monotonic-safe stub, not allocator instrumentation.

node-smol has no JS-addressable buffer-handle concept — the back buffer is a C++-internal reference consumed in-process by the renderer* draw methods, never handed to JS as its own handle the way stuie's buffer registry does. Pending on the buffer-handle tier (createOptimizedBuffer and the buffer* family), without which there is no handle for this to return.

node-smol's Renderer tracks no timing, frame-count, or cells-updated statistics, and there is no packed-stats readback of any kind. Pending on a diagnostics tier: stuie's own docs list Diagnostics as a first-class FFI category (docs/interop-and-performance.md:276), and these are real production numbers (OpenTUI's CliRenderer stats overlay), so no sanctioned out-of-scope reason applies — not audio, not bun:ffi-shaped (a packed Uint8Array out-param is exactly node-smol's existing idiom, cf. rendererFlush's caller-supplied dst), not harness-only.

stuie's Renderer persists a `background: [u16;4]` that auto-clears both buffers on create, resize, and after every render; node-smol's Renderer stores no background at all — rendererClear takes an explicit color on every call, so the "implicit renderer background" capability does not exist. Pending on the renderer-state tier alongside setRenderOffset/setUseThread.
